name: Poppy
grown_as: The wild common poppy, a hardy annual of disturbed ground. William's library also has a poppy from Bristol Botanic Garden whose species is not given. ⚠️ CHECK what the Bristol Botanic Garden poppy is.
habit: A branched annual 30 to 60 cm tall, the stems and stalks covered in stiff spreading hairs; a leafy base with long, thin, wavering flower stalks above. All parts bleed white milky sap when cut.

leaf.arrangement: A loose rosette at first, then alternate up the stem
leaf.type: Simple but deeply cut: pinnately divided almost to the midrib into narrow, toothed lobes
leaf.outline: Oblong to lance-shaped overall, 5 to 15 cm long
leaf.base: Lower leaves narrow into a stalk; upper leaves stalkless
leaf.tip: The end lobe longer and pointed
leaf.margin: Each lobe edged with coarse, sharp, bristle-tipped teeth
leaf.veins: A clear midrib running up the middle with a vein into each lobe
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves stalked, upper ones without

flower.form: A large open bowl of four papery, crumpled-looking petals
flower.petals: Four, free, very broad and rounded, overlapping: two large outer ones and two slightly smaller inner ones
flower.colour: Scarlet, often with a black blotch at the base of each petal
flower.centre: A flat-topped green seed box with a disc of 8 to 12 dark rays on top, ringed by a mass of dark purple-black stamens
flower.behind: No sepals show: the two hairy sepals fall as the flower opens
flower.carried: Alone at the top of a long, thin, hairy stalk; the hairy bud hangs down, then the stalk straightens and the flower faces up

fruit: A smooth hairless capsule, round to broadly egg-shaped, 1 to 2 cm, with a flat lid of 8 to 12 rays; green ripening grey-brown, shaking out seed from a ring of small holes under the lid. Seeds tiny (about 1 mm), kidney-shaped, dark grey to black, with a fine net pattern.
seedling: Two narrow strap-shaped, greyish seed leaves, then small spoon-shaped first leaves that soon become lobed and toothed
winter: None: an annual. Autumn-sown seedlings sit as small rosettes over winter.

leaf: leaf deeply cut into narrow toothed lobes along a midrib
bloom: four broad overlapping scarlet petals forming a bowl
black blotches at the petal bases
a green seed box with a rayed lid ringed by dark stamens
seedling: first true leaves spoon-shaped, starting to lobe
young: a loose rosette of deeply cut, toothed, hairy leaves
flower: single scarlet flowers on long thin hairy stalks
seedhead: round smooth capsules with a flat rayed lid on tall thin stalks

look_alikes: Long-headed poppy (Papaver dubium) is paler orange-red without black blotches and has a long narrow capsule. Prickly poppy and rough poppy have bristly capsules. Opium poppy is grey and hairless with clasping leaves and big lilac or white flowers.
